messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Air: one more constants row, the one only a long literal can test.** The funnel ports `FloatDecimal`, whose buffer holds 800 digits plus a `truncated` flag, and that flag decides a tie when digits are dropped (`sawc/std/float.saw` ~2257: "The tie — a lone `5` with nothing after it — is where `truncated` earns" its place). None of the listed values exceeds 800 digits AND sits on a tie, so a port that drops the flag would pass the whole matrix. Add a literal on the halfway point between two doubles with a nonzero digit past the buffer: `9007199254740993.` followed by 800 zeros and a `1`. That must round UP to `9007199254740994` (`…994`); the same text without the final `1` ties to even, `…992`. Both bit patterns come from the Stage 0 oracle (Python `float()`).

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: Verified on SL-722.p1 (U2): `air-review/sl722/tie.saw` is byte-identical to Stage 0 at -O0 and -O2 (the 817-digit tie rounds up, its twin ties to even, and the run-time `a*b+c` stays 0 with no fast-math flag in the IR). Resolving; the plan text can carry the row whenever it is next revised.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Air: state the no-fast-math invariant here, and pin it at -O2.** IEEE results depend on the backend emitting NO fast-math flags (`nnan`, `ninf`, `nsz`, `arcp`, `contract`, `afn`, `reassoc`) on any Float instruction, and never contracting a multiply-add into `fma`. A row that catches a regression: `func mul_add(a: Float, b: Float, c: Float) -> Float { a * b + c }` called with RUNTIME operands `(0.1, 10.0, -1.0)`. Stage 0 gives bits `0` at both `-O0` and `-O2` (`air-review/floatdoc/s0_rows.saw`); a fused multiply-add gives about `5.55e-17`. Run-time parameters keep LLVM from folding it at compile time, so the row tests the emitted instructions.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Air: add the NaN rows to this reaching position.** `Set<Float>` after inserting one NaN twice, then `0.0` and `-0.0`: Stage 0 says `len 3`, `contains(nan) false`, `contains(0.0) true` (`air-review/floatdoc/s0_rows.saw`). NaN is never equal to itself, so each insert adds an entry and no lookup finds one, while the zeros hash alike and merge. That pins `equals` and `hash` together at the cell where they disagree with bit equality, which the ±0 row alone does not.

anchor.exact: A generic ordering operator then lowers per instance

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Air: the lean needs a MIR-level change, worth naming in U3.** Today the generic ordering operator is desugared in MIR itself (`le<T>` is `Ne(compare(a, b), Greater)`, as this section says), and MIR is lowered once per generic, before mono knows the instance. "Lowers per instance" therefore means MIR keeps a generic ordering operator as its own node (an `Order(op, a, b)` rvalue, or the existing compare call marked as an ordering operator) that mono expands: `fcmp` at a scalar instance, the `compare` desugaring otherwise. Without that node the lean cannot be built in mono alone. Whichever unit owns it should say so, and the g01 row is its pin.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: Observed on SL-722.p3 r2: with Float's `compare` lowered, a generic `le<T: Comparable>` answers `true` for `nan <= 1.0` (Stage 0: `false`), at -O0 and -O2. The cell compiles before Q3 rules. My review of SL-722.p3 asks either to keep it refused until the ruling, or to get Q3 ruled and lower a marked `<=`/`>=` per instance.
